title: Podgora Itinerary 2027: 1, 3 and 5 Day Plans
metaDescription: Plan Podgora, Croatia in 2027: day-by-day itineraries, beaches, Biokovo Skywalk, Hvar ferry from Drvenik, costs in euros, and local tips.
content:
## How Many Days Do You Need in Podgora?

Podgora sits on the Makarska Riviera, between Makarska (about 8 km north) and Igrane (about 5 km south). Split is roughly 75 km away, and Split Airport is about 1 hour by road. Three days covers the town, Biokovo and the nearby beaches. Five days adds island trips. One day works only as a stop on a longer coastal drive.

Peak season runs from June to September. Sea temperatures are comfortable for swimming from late May to early October. July and August are the busiest and hottest months, so plan hikes for early morning.

## Podgora Itinerary at a Glance

| Day | Focus | Main stops |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Town and beach | Promenade, harbour, pebble beach, Wings monument, sunset swim |
| 2 | Biokovo | Nature Park gate, Skywalk, Podbiokovlje villages |
| 3 | Coast | Igrane, Brela, Punta Rata, Makarska old town |
| 4 | Islands | Hvar via Drvenik–Sućuraj ferry, or Brač |
| 5 | Slow day | Kayaking, Igrane–Blato trail, long lunch |

## Day 1: Podgora Town, Harbour and Beach

Start on the pine-shaded seafront promenade, which connects the harbour with the town's pebble beaches. The water is clear, and the beach shelves quickly, so it suits confident swimmers more than toddlers. Water shoes help on the pebbles.

The Wings monument above the town is a large concrete memorial to local Second World War history. It is a short drive or an uphill walk of about 30–40 minutes, and it gives a wide view over the channel toward Brač and Hvar. The parish church dedicated to All Saints is also in the town centre.

Finish with dinner by the harbour. Fresh fish is usually sold by weight, so ask the price before ordering. A grilled fish plate typically costs €18–30 per person, and a pasta or risotto starter costs €10–15.

## Day 2: Biokovo Nature Park and the Skywalk

Biokovo is the highest and longest mountain range in Dalmatia, and Podgora is one of the closest towns to its main gate. The Skywalk Biokovo is a glass walkway at 1,228 m above sea level, and it was the first of its kind in Croatia.

Three ways to reach it:

- **Guided cabrio bus tour:** From about €65 per person, with morning and sunset departures. It has a 4.8 rating on major booking platforms.
- **Quad or buggy tour from Makarska:** From about €75–€100 per person depending on the season. Rated 4.7.
- **Own car:** The road up is narrow and winding with steep drop-offs. Allow about 45 minutes from the coast, and arrive before 10:00 in summer to avoid slow traffic.

The temperature at the top is often 8–12°C lower than on the coast, so bring a light jacket even in July. Closed shoes are needed on gravel paths.

The Kotišina Botanical Garden is also inside the park and is worth a short stop if you want a quiet nature walk rather than a viewpoint.

### A Lower-Effort Alternative: Podbiokovlje Villages

The circular trail from Podgora to Podbiokovlje takes 2–2.5 hours and returns via Srida Sela. It is rated moderate, with old stone hamlets and olive groves. Go in the morning, take 1.5 litres of water, and avoid midday heat.

## Day 3: Igrane, Brela and Makarska

Drive south for 5 km to Igrane, a small village with a quiet shoreline and fewer crowds than Makarska. In the other direction, Brela is about 12 km north. Its Punta Rata beach, with the Brela Rock (Kamen Brela) offshore, is the most photographed beach on the riviera.

Punta Rata is crowded from 11:00 to 17:00 in July and August. Arrive before 09:30 or after 17:00. Parking in Brela is limited and pay-and-display, usually €2–4 per hour in summer.

On the way back, spend the evening in Makarska. The old town and main square are compact, and the seafront promenade is lively until late.

## Day 4: Island Day Trip to Hvar or Brač

The Drvenik–Sućuraj ferry to eastern Hvar is the practical option from Podgora. Drvenik is about 15 km south, and the crossing takes about 35 minutes. Foot passengers pay roughly €4–5, and a car costs about €20–25 one way. In July and August, queue by 07:00 for early sailings, or go as a foot passenger and rent a scooter or taxi on the island.

Sućuraj is at the far east end of Hvar, so Hvar Town is a long drive of more than 70 km. Skip a same-day trip to Hvar Town unless you leave very early. The better plan is to stay on eastern Hvar, or choose Brač instead (Makarska–Sumartin ferry, about 1 hour).

Boat tours from Makarska to nearby islands, including a three-island speedboat trip, are another option if you do not want to bring a car.

## Day 5: Slow Coastal Day

Use the last day for an easier trail: the Igrane–Blato route is rated easy at 4.7 and takes about 3–3.5 hours. Sea kayaking at sunset is available through local operators along the Podgora seafront. End with lunch at a konoba in the hills above the coast, where lamb, peka (slow-cooked meat and vegetables under a bell) and local wine cost less than at the harbour.

## Getting Around

- **Car:** The most flexible option. Rental from Split Airport costs about €40–80 per day in summer. Book early for July and August.
- **Bus:** Regular coastal buses connect Podgora with Makarska and Split. Single fares to Makarska are about €2–3 and to Split about €8–12.
- **Walking:** The town is flat and compact, and the promenade can be walked end to end in about 20 minutes.
- **Ferries:** Drvenik (Hvar line) and Makarska (Brač line) are both within a 30-minute drive.

## Where to Stay

Podgora has private apartments, family-run guesthouses and several beachfront hotels. Apartments are the best value for groups. Expect around €60–110 per night in July and August for a two-person unit, and €35–60 in May, June and September. Choose a place within 200 m of the seafront if you do not have a car.

## Local Tips

- Swim early. The sea is calmest before 10:00, and the afternoon wind (maestral) can make it choppy.
- Buy supplies at a supermarket in Podgora or Makarska. Beach cafés charge about €3–4 for a coffee and €4–6 for a beer.
- Cash is still useful at small konobas and parking machines, though most restaurants take cards.
- Book Skywalk tours a day or two ahead in peak season. Sunset slots fill first.
- The mountain road can be closed in strong wind or fire-risk periods. Check with the tour operator or the Biokovo Nature Park office on the morning of your trip.

## Best Time to Visit

May, June and September give the best balance of warm sea, lower prices and fewer people. July and August are best for beach life but demand early starts for hikes and ferries. Visiting from November to March means most seasonal restaurants are closed, though hiking in Biokovo remains possible on clear days.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Podgora?
faq.answer: Three days covers the town, the Biokovo Skywalk and nearby beaches. Five days lets you add an island trip to Hvar or Brač and an easy coastal hike.

faq.question: What is the best thing to do in Podgora?
faq.answer: The Biokovo Skywalk at 1,228 m is the main highlight, with views over the Makarska Riviera and islands. For a simple day, the pebble beach and promenade are the core of the town.

faq.question: How much does a Biokovo Skywalk tour cost?
faq.answer: Guided cabrio bus tours start at about €65 per person, and quad tours at about €75–€100. Prices vary by season and group size.

faq.question: How far is Podgora from Makarska and Split?
faq.answer: Podgora is about 8 km from Makarska, a 10-minute drive. Split is roughly 75 km away, about 1 hour by car.

faq.question: Is Podgora good for a beach holiday?
faq.answer: Yes. It has pebble beaches with clear water, a shaded promenade and calmer surroundings than Makarska. Neighbouring Brela and Tučepi add more beach options within 15 minutes.

faq.question: How do you get from Podgora to Hvar?
faq.answer: Drive about 15 km south to Drvenik and take the ferry to Sućuraj on eastern Hvar, a crossing of about 35 minutes. Foot passengers pay roughly €4–5 and cars about €20–25, with long queues in July and August.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Podgora?
faq.answer: Late May, June and September offer warm sea and lower prices. July and August are the hottest and busiest months.

quickAnswer: A good Podgora itinerary lasts 3 to 5 days. Spend day 1 on the town promenade and pebble beaches, day 2 hiking or driving up Biokovo to the Skywalk (1,228 m), day 3 in Igrane and Brela, and add a Hvar or Brač ferry trip on days 4–5. Peak season is June to September.
